property_summary: An address that is not an approved logger returns true from approvedToLog, while an approved logger returns false.

For any logger address, the result of approvedToLog must equal the approvedLoggers state mapping; the buggy version returns false regardless of the mapping, violating this for any address that has been approved.
After any call to setApprovedLogger, the value of approvedLoggers for the given address must equal the input status; the mutant inverts it so they differ.

After two consecutive calls to setApprovedLogger with the same address and the same status parameter, the final value of approvedLoggers for that address must equal the original value (idempotency under same status); the mutant inverts the status on each call, so the second call flips it back to the opposite of the original.
After calling setApprovedLogger with status=false, the approvedLoggers mapping for that address must be false; the mutant inverts the status and sets it to true.

After calling setApprovedLogger with two different addresses consecutively, the approvedLoggers value for the first address must not be affected by the second call; the mutant inverts the status for every call, so calling setApprovedLogger for another address also flips the status of the previously set logger if the same status argument is used.

For any two distinct addresses A and B and any boolean status, after calling setApprovedLogger(A, status) and then setApprovedLogger(B, status), the value of approvedLoggers(A) must equal status; the mutant inverts both assignments so for some status approvedLoggers(A) differs.
For any caller authorized by onlyOwner, setApprovedLogger must set the logger status to the value provided as _status; the mutant always sets it to true, violating this rule when _status is false.

For any approved logger and any boolean, a call to setApprovedLogger must set the logger's approved status to that boolean; the mutant ignores the boolean and always sets it to true, so after a call with false the logger remains approved.

For any address that is not approved to log, after a call to setApprovedLogger with _status=false the logger must NOT become approved; the mutant always sets it to true, so an unapproved address can become approved even when _status is false.

For any address k and boolean s, if owner calls setApprovedLogger(k,s) then (s == true) implies approvedLoggers(k) must be true; the mutant makes approvedLoggers(k) true regardless of s, so when s is false and k was unapproved before, the reference leaves k unapproved while the mutant makes k approved.

For any address k and any boolean _status, after the owner calls setApprovedLogger(k, _status), the caller-approvedToLog(k) must equal _status; the mutant always sets it to true, so after a call with _status=false the owner can still observe approvedToLog(k)==true.
For any logger address, calling setApprovedLogger with _status=true must result in approvedLoggers[logger] being true, but the mutant always sets it to false, violating this expectation.

After any call to setApprovedLogger, the value of approvedLoggers for the given logger address equals the status argument; the mutant never updates the mapping so the rule fails for any call where _status differs from the initial false.

For any two distinct loggers, after calling setApprovedLogger for the first logger with status true, the first logger becomes approved while the second logger remains unapproved; the mutant never updates the mapping so the second logger incorrectly shows as approved when the owner sets its status.

After owner calls setApprovedLogger for any address with any boolean status, the mapping approvedLoggers for that address equals the status; the mutant never writes to the mapping so approvedLoggers stays false regardless of status.
After the owner calls setApprovedLogger(_logger, _status), if _status is true then _logger must be approved; the bug never writes to the mapping so no logger ever becomes approved.

After the owner calls setApprovedLogger multiple times, the final approvedLoggers value for any address equals the last status set for that address; the mutant never writes so any non-default status assignment is lost, causing a mismatch when a later call queries the mapping.

After any call to setApprovedLogger, the set of approved loggers should only depend on the explicit parameters given; the mutant always sets address(0) to true, violating that for inputs where _status is false and _logger is not address(0).

Calling setApprovedLogger twice with the same _logger but different _status values always results in the same final approvedLoggers state for any key other than _logger; the mutant forces address(0) to true on the second call, making its state differ from the reference when the second call's _status is false.

For any call to setApprovedLogger, the resulting state change for approvedLoggers is exactly that the key equal to the first argument is set to the second argument, and no other key's value changes; the mutant additionally sets approvedLoggers[address(0)] to true regardless of the arguments, causing a state difference for any call where address(0) was not already true.

For any call to setApprovedLogger, the difference between the number of approved loggers before and after must be at most 1; the buggy version can increase the count by 2 (setting both the given logger and address(0) to true) when address(0) was previously false.

For any call to setApprovedLogger, the resulting approvedLoggers state for a key other than the given _logger depends only on its previous state for that key; the bug always sets address(0) to true, changing its state independently of _status when _logger != address(0).

For any address _logger and bool _status, after a call to setApprovedLogger(_logger, _status), the value of approvedLoggers(_logger) must equal _status. In the buggy version, approvedLoggers(_logger) remains unchanged while approvedLoggers(msg.sender) is set instead.
